html:
SMTO-SKL-0121 — Slack needs you to connect your account again

GUID: 5e980636-8402-5f5d-941e-7e9732556082
Slug: slack-reauthorization-required
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Slack no longer accepts SMTO's saved sign-in for this connection. It may have expired, been revoked, or been disconnected. Slack didn't carry out this request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to list your Slack workspaces. Note the workspace key (the name the connection is saved under) of the one that failed. Reconnecting under that exact key keeps the same connection instead of making a new one.
  2. Ask the Agent to connect Slack with the same Slack OAuth App and that workspace key. Open the link it gives you and approve the request in Slack. A fresh approval gives SMTO a new working sign-in; an expired or interrupted one can't be reused.
  3. If connecting fails straight away, open Parameter Store, open your Slack OAuth App entry, and check that its client ID and client secret match your Slack app. Slack also refuses the sign-in when the app's ID or secret is wrong.
  4. Once Slack shows as connected, ask the Agent for your request again. Slack refused the request because the sign-in wasn't accepted, so it's safe to repeat after reconnecting.

What success looks like

  • The Agent reports Slack as connected and your request completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your Slack app for SMTO. Don't paste your Slack client secret or any sign-in codes into a conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack rejected or could not refresh the saved access token (invalid_auth, token_revoked, token_expired, account_inactive, HTTP 401 or a failed OAuth code exchange), or the slack_workspace profile's authorization_state is not available.

What this means

  • HTTP/token responses report invalid, expired, revoked or inactive authorization, or saved token-rotation state is unavailable. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • HTTP/token responses report invalid, expired, revoked or inactive authorization, or saved token-rotation state is unavailable.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact authorization or rotation state rather than substituting a different token.

How to fix it

  • Run slack.connect with the same auth_app_ref and workspace_key to get fresh consent; an interrupted token rotation deliberately leaves authorization_state=reauthorization_required and is never retried. If the code exchange itself fails, verify the Slack OAuth App profile's client_id and client_secret and that the registered HTTPS callback (/api/agent/slack/oauth/callback) matches the Server origin.
  • Run slack.connect for the exact app and workspace key. An interrupted or rejected token rotation requires fresh consent.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Fresh consent restores the same intended app/workspace/principal grant.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
